View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1140

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Monday! Today, we’re diving into Bank of America hiring 1,000 contractors to patch the flaws Anthropic’s Mythos [ https://substack.com/redirect/964e8f6b-2cdb-4b70-aa9a-dbce577cc862?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] found - the first real numbers on what defending against AI costs a bank (why those contractors don’t show up in BofA’s falling headcount, why the “couple hundred million plus” Q3 bill is blended with AML fixes, and what’s worth watching next + bonus deep dive into a16z’s State of Markets 2026: The AI Playbook for Founders and Investors [ https://substack.com/redirect/d7f80043-6e16-4754-a592-0c25622ab222?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and The Agentic Transition Playbook [ https://substack.com/redirect/4eb71c23-dcf0-4c75-9644-0909ac7e23b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), breaking down OpenAI UK’s 2025 accounts to see what they tell us about the real price of frontier AI talent (why London’s £20.3M “profit” is a fee the US parent sets, why UK’s turnover now moves with OpenAI’s valuation, & what to watch next + bonus deep dives into OpenAI [ https://substack.com/redirect/b244a354-1a31-4777-8709-119e2506057e?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] and The Top 10 Stocks Positioned to Benefit Most from Anthropic IPO [ https://substack.com/redirect/932b02b0-e57b-4179-88f3-77d921fcc17c?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and exploring why Citibank is now following JPMorgan in blocking AI agents from customer accounts (what the banks are really protecting here, why regulators are quietly on their side, and what to watch next + bonus deep dive into How to Hire a Grok Bot: Your First AI Employee [ https://substack.com/redirect/969ced35-429f-4785-bf7e-bf09c7573d55?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside) So let’s jump straight into the good stuff 🌶️
Bank of America just put the first number on what defending against AI costs a bank 🤖💸
Following the money 💸 Banking giant Bank of America $BAC  is the first major bank to put numbers on the cost of defending against Anthropic’s Mythos [ https://substack.com/redirect/964e8f6b-2cdb-4b70-aa9a-dbce577cc862?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], the AI model that has exposed decades-old flaws in bank and vendor code faster than teams can patch them.
Set against the bank’s AI savings targets, CEO Brian Moynihan’s figures complicate the bank’s own AI efficiency story. Part of the defense bill sits on a line investors don’t track, and the backlog he says will clear is moving more slowly than attackers.

81079.subject: How Avalanche Is Becoming Infrastructure for South Korea’s Onchain Capital Markets
81079.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/how-avalanche-is-becoming-infrastructure

Tokenization is beginning to move beyond individual assets and into the infrastructure of capital markets themselves.
South Korea is approaching that transition by changing the legal and technical systems that determine how securities can be issued, recorded and managed. In January 2026, its National Assembly passed amendments to the Electronic Registration Act and the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, establishing a legal framework for securities issued using distributed ledgers.
The legislation takes effect on February 4, 2027. Its initial implementation will focus on selected institutional financial products, unlisted stocks and fractional investment securities, with plans to expand into conventional publicly offered securities as the market develops.
The Korea Securities Depository (KSD) is developing infrastructure designed to connect with Avalanche, Hyperledger Fabric and Hyperledger Besu. Meanwhile, Hanwha Investment & Securities has completed a token securities platform [ https://substack.com/redirect/7d3b6f18-ec77-499d-803e-e9e62f525ead?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] supporting Avalanche and Hyperledger Besu, positioning itself ahead of the regulatory framework’s launch.
These developments offer an early look at how blockchain could become part of South Korea’s regulated securities infrastructure.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
From electronic securities to onchain markets
South Korea has made a major transition in securities infrastructure before.
In 2019, the country introduced its electronic securities system, replacing physical certificates for listed stocks and bonds with electronically registered records. KSD became central to that infrastructure, maintaining registration records and supporting the management of securities ownership rights.
The new framework extends that evolution by allowing distributed ledgers to serve as part of the legally recognized recordkeeping system. Tokenized securities will remain subject to existing capital markets laws, including requirements around financial investment activities, disclosure and investor protection.
This creates a path for financial institutions to incorporate blockchain into established securities processes while operating within Korea’s regulatory framework. The transition will happen gradually, beginning with selected financial products.
According to the Financial Services Commission’s September roadmap, the first phase beginning in February 2027 will cover privately pooled money market funds and bonds for institutional investors, unlisted stocks issued through trust structures, and publicly offered fractional investment securities.

## DeepSeek still thinks it's ChatGPT

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ac84a150-a352-4c28-be8a-5ad1121e7a92/cdda1692-84d2-45ff-84b8-62ebcbca1461.jpg?t=1792395170)
Caption: 

Ask DeepSeek who it is, and it might tell you it's ChatGPT.

One X user tried it 30 times on Saturday, and DeepSeek called itself ChatGPT in 26 of them.

A fingerprint test going around online also [claims DeepSeek's new model looks a lot like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra](https://www.techflowpost.com/en-US/article/34668).

It's done this before.

* In 2024, DeepSeek V3 called itself ChatGPT in 5 of 8 tries and even told some of GPT-4's jokes, punchlines included.

* In February, Anthropic said DeepSeek used fake accounts to pull more than 150,000 answers out of Claude.

* OpenAI's terms ban using its answers to build a competing model.

Training one AI on another AI's answers is called distillation. A chatbot getting its own name wrong doesn't prove it, since the internet is packed with ChatGPT's writing.

People online joked that DeepSeek must have switched teachers after Anthropic called it out for copying Claude.
